router_distinctions:
Pick the tier that best balances capability and cost.

codex-fast: ONLY for trivial mechanical actions with no reasoning — greetings, toggling, listing, single-fact lookups. If the user asks WHY, HOW, or needs any judgment, explanation, or synthesis, do NOT use codex-fast.

codex-dev: Default for most work — questions, research, code, debugging, writing, summaries, web search, multi-step tasks.

codex-arch: Architecture, deep trade-offs, large refactors, building new modules from scratch.

agent: ONLY when the user explicitly requests parallel independent workstreams. Most tasks, even complex ones, should go to a single-model tier.

tiers.name: codex-fast
tiers.router_label: Greetings, small talk, yes/no questions, single-fact lookups (weather, time, date), toggling a setting on/off, running an existing scheduled job, listing items (files, jobs, skills, settings)

tiers.name: codex-dev
tiers.router_label: Any question requiring explanation or reasoning, summarizing content, translations, web search and synthesis, code review, debugging, reading logs, editing files, implementing features, fixing bugs, writing scripts and tests, multi-file changes, creating scheduled jobs and reminders, research, multi-step sequential tasks

tiers.name: codex-arch
tiers.router_label: Architecture design, system-level reasoning, complex trade-off analysis, large-scale refactoring, implementing complex features, redesigning system architecture, building new modules from scratch, complex multi-step tasks requiring deep thinking

tiers.name: agent
tiers.router_label: ONLY for tasks explicitly requesting a team of agents, or requiring parallel independent workstreams that CANNOT be done sequentially by one model (e.g. 'build a full app with frontend + backend + tests simultaneously', 'write 5 articles at once', 'research 3 topics in parallel'). If one model can handle it step-by-step, use codex-dev or codex-arch instead.
